entries.black-sea-cucumber: Can detach and regrow its internal organs when stressed, a process called evisceration.
entries.teatfish-sea-cucumber: One of the most commercially valuable sea cucumber species, sold as beche-de-mer.
entries.red-sea-cucumber: Uses tube feet along its underside to slowly crawl across the seafloor.
entries.christmas-tree-worm: Can retract its colorful spiral plumes into its tube in less than a second.
entries.giant-tubeworm: Has no mouth, stomach, or gut, relying entirely on symbiotic bacteria for nutrition.
entries.feather-duster-worm: Its feathery crown of tentacles is used for both feeding and respiration.
entries.bearded-fireworm: Has hollow, venom-filled bristles that cause intense burning pain on contact.
entries.blue-glaucus: Floats upside-down on the surface tension of the water, using stored air bubbles.
entries.spanish-dancer: Named for its spectacular undulating swimming motion that resembles a flamenco dancer.
entries.leaf-sheep: Is one of the only animals capable of photosynthesis, stealing chloroplasts from algae.
entries.sea-butterfly: Swims by flapping its wing-like shell extensions, resembling a butterfly in flight.
entries.sea-angel: Is a shell-less snail that swims with graceful wing-like movements.
entries.sea-hare: Can release a cloud of purple ink when threatened, confusing predators.
entries.giant-clam: Can weigh over 500 pounds and live for more than 100 years.
entries.geoduck: Can live for over 160 years, making it one of the longest-living animals on Earth.
entries.atlantic-surf-clam: Can propel itself out of the sand using its muscular foot when disturbed.
entries.bay-scallop: Can swim short distances by rapidly clapping its shell valves together.
entries.blue-mussel: Attaches to rocks using strong byssal threads, forming dense beds of thousands.
entries.thorny-oyster: Shell is covered in long, sharp spines that deter predators.
entries.lion-paw-scallop: Named for its ridged, colorful shell that resembles a lion's paw.
entries.nautilus-pompilius: Shell follows a logarithmic spiral, one of nature's most perfect mathematical forms.
entries.paper-nautilus: Females create a delicate, paper-thin shell for egg protection.
entries.atlantic-horseshoe-crab: Has been virtually unchanged for 450 million years, predating the dinosaurs.
entries.japanese-horseshoe-crab: Its blue blood contains Limulus Amebocyte Lysate, used to test for bacterial contamination in medical equipment.
entries.indo-pacific-horseshoe-crab: Is the only horseshoe crab species found in Asian coastal waters.
entries.sea-squirt-tunicate: Is more closely related to vertebrates than most invertebrates, being a chordate.
entries.marine-flatworm: Can regenerate an entire organism from a fragment as small as 1/200th of its body.
entries.sea-pen-glow: Produces bioluminescent waves that travel along its colony when physically disturbed.
entries.dodo: The dodo was a flightless bird from Mauritius that went extinct in the late 17th century due to hunting and invasive species.
entries.woolly-mammoth: Woolly mammoths coexisted with early humans and their remains are still found frozen in Siberian permafrost.
entries.passenger-pigeon: Passenger pigeons once numbered in the billions and their flocks would darken the sky for hours as they flew overhead.
entries.tasmanian-tiger: Despite being called a tiger, it was actually a marsupial more closely related to kangaroos than to big cats.
entries.quagga: The quagga was half-zebra, half-horse with stripes only on the front half of its body. The last one died in 1883.

entries.vampire-bat: Only mammal that feeds entirely on blood
entries.tree-kangaroo: Lives in trees despite being a kangaroo
entries.quokka: Known as the happiest animal on Earth
entries.quoll: Native to Australia and New Guinea
entries.numbat: Eats up to 20000 termites per day
entries.fisher: One of few animals that can kill porcupines
entries.pine-marten: Can rotate its hind feet to climb down trees
entries.weasel: Can squeeze through holes as small as 2cm
entries.star-nosed-mole: Can identify and eat food in under 230 milliseconds
entries.chinese-pangolin: Most trafficked mammal in the world
entries.sunda-pangolin: Curls into a ball when threatened
entries.indian-pangolin: Has no teeth but uses strong stomach muscles
entries.giant-armadillo: Can destroy termite mounds with one swipe
entries.nine-banded-armadillo: Always gives birth to identical quadruplets
entries.southern-three-banded-armadillo: Can roll into a complete ball
entries.two-toed-sloth: Moves so slowly that algae grows on its fur
entries.aardvark: Only living species in its order
entries.bat-eared-fox: Uses large ears to locate insects underground
entries.spotted-hyena: Has one of the strongest bite forces
entries.striped-hyena: Has a mane of hair along its spine
entries.raccoon-dog: Not actually a raccoon or a dog
entries.crabeater-seal: Most abundant seal species in the world
entries.weddell-seal: Can dive for over an hour
entries.ross-seal: Rarely seen due to remote habitat
entries.arctic-ground-squirrel: Can supercool its blood to below freezing
entries.springhare: Can jump up to 2 meters high
entries.paca: Has distinctive white spots along its sides
entries.rock-hyrax: Closest living relative to the elephant
entries.hyrax: Related to elephants despite its size
entries.fennec-foxes: Has oversized ears for heat dissipation
entries.blanford-s-fox: Can jump up to 3 meters vertically
entries.r-ppell-s-fox: Named after German naturalist Eduard Rüppell
entries.ussuri-brown-bear: Largest bear in Europe and Asia
entries.kodiak-bear: One of the largest bear subspecies
entries.syrian-brown-bear: Smallest of the brown bear subspecies
entries.atlantic-walrus: Tusks can grow up to 1 meter
entries.pacific-walrus: Uses tusks to haul out on ice
entries.guadalupe-fur-seal: Was once hunted to near extinction
entries.new-zealand-sea-lion: One of the rarest sea lions
entries.galapagos-sea-lion: Only lives on the Galapagos Islands
entries.south-american-sea-lion: Males have thick manes of hair
entries.antarctic-fur-seal: Has dense fur with up to 300000 hairs per square centimeter
entries.pangolin: Most trafficked mammal in the world
entries.yellow-throated-marten: Can prey on animals larger than itself
entries.short-eared-dog: Only canid in South America's rainforests
entries.bush-dog: Lives in pack of up to 12
entries.sechuran-fox: Found only in Peru and Ecuador
entries.siamese-fox: Also called the Asian raccoon dog
entries.kit-fox: Largest ears relative to body size
entries.island-fox: Found only on California's Channel Islands
entries.bat-eared-foxes: Uses large ears to locate insects underground
entries.reeves-s-muntjac: Introduced to the UK from China
entries.pere-david-s-deer: Extinct in the wild, survives only in captivity
entries.red-deer: Largest deer species in the world
entries.reindeer: Only deer species where both sexes have antlers
entries.red-tailed-hawk: Red-tailed hawks are often dubbed over other raptors in movies because of their piercing scream.
entries.great-horned-owl: Great horned owls have a grip strength of about 300 psi, comparable to a large dogs bite.
entries.snowy-owl: Unlike most owls, snowy owls are diurnal and hunt during daylight hours.
entries.northern-saw-whet-owl: The northern saw-whet owl is one of the smallest owls in North America, weighing less than a soda can.
entries.barred-owl: Barred owls are known for their distinctive call that sounds like Who cooks for you.
entries.long-eared-owl: Long-eared owls have asymmetric ear openings that allow them to pinpoint prey in complete darkness.
entries.great-gray-owl: The great gray owl is the tallest owl in North America, though much of its size is feathers.
entries.burrowing-owl: Burrowing owls nest underground in burrows dug by prairie dogs or ground squirrels.
entries.elf-owl: The elf owl is the smallest owl species in the world, weighing less than a ping pong ball.
entries.wood-duck: Wood ducklings can jump from tree nests up to 50 feet high without injury.
entries.northern-pintail: The northern pintails long tail makes it one of the most elegant ducks in flight.
entries.green-winged-teal: The green-winged teal is the smallest dabbling duck in North America.
entries.canvasback: The canvasback is the largest and fastest diving duck in North America.
entries.snow-goose: Snow goose flocks can number in the hundreds of thousands during migration.
entries.greylag-goose: The greylag goose is the ancestor of most domestic goose breeds in Europe.
entries.trumpeter-swan: The trumpeter swan is the heaviest bird native to North America.
entries.tundra-swan: Tundra swans migrate up to 4,000 miles each way between Arctic breeding grounds and wintering areas.
entries.american-robin: American robins can eat 14 feet of earthworms in a single day.
entries.northern-cardinal: Northern cardinal females also sing, which is rare among North American songbirds.
entries.american-crow: American crows can recognize individual human faces and hold grudges.
entries.common-raven: Ravens can slide down snow-covered roofs for fun and perform aerial acrobatics.
entries.house-sparrow: House sparrows were introduced to North America in 1851 and have since spread across the continent.
entries.european-robin: The European robin is a symbol of Christmas in Britain and appears on many holiday cards.
entries.eastern-bluebird: Eastern bluebirds can see ultraviolet light, which helps them find ripe berries.
entries.western-bluebird: Western bluebirds are one of the few songbirds that nest in old woodpecker holes.
entries.baltimore-oriole: Baltimore orioles weave intricate hanging nests that can take up to two weeks to build.
entries.scarlet-tanager: The male scarlet tanager turns olive-green in winter, looking like a completely different bird.
entries.yellow-warbler: Yellow warblers are one of the first songbirds to arrive on their breeding grounds in spring.
entries.white-throated-sparrow: White-throated sparrows come in two color morphs that pair almost exclusively with each other.
entries.dark-eyed-junco: Dark-eyed juncos are called snowbirds because they appear in southern states during winter.
entries.ruby-throated-hummingbird: Ruby-throated hummingbirds beat their wings 53 times per second and can fly backwards.
entries.annas-hummingbird: Male Annas hummingbirds perform dramatic diving displays that create an audible chirp.
entries.black-chinned-hummingbird: The black chin of this hummingbird flashes brilliant purple when the light hits it at the right angle.
entries.belted-kingfisher: The belted kingfisher is one of the few bird species where females are more colorful than males.
entries.great-blue-heron: Great blue herons can stand motionless for hours waiting for the perfect moment to strike prey.
entries.great-egret: The great egrets long plumes nearly drove it to extinction in the 19th century for use in womens hats.
entries.snowy-egret: Snowy egrets use their bright yellow feet to stir up prey from muddy bottoms.
entries.green-heron: Green herons are one of the few bird species that use tools, dropping bait on the water to attract fish.
entries.american-flamingo: American flamingos are the most brightly colored of all flamingo species.
entries.sandhill-crane: Sandhill cranes perform elaborate dances that include jumping, bowing, and tossing sticks.
entries.whooping-crane: Whooping cranes were once down to only 15 birds in the wild, making them one of the rarest birds in North America.
entries.purple-gallinule: Purple gallinules can walk across lily pads thanks to their extremely long toes.
entries.american-coot: American coots can sink slowly into water to hide, submerging up to their necks.
entries.wild-turkey: Wild turkeys can fly at speeds up to 55 mph and run at 25 mph.
entries.ring-necked-pheasant: Male ring-necked pheasants have such vivid plumage that they were once used as models for dragon illustrations.
entries.bobwhite-quail: The northern bobwhite is named for its distinctive two-note call that sounds like its name.
entries.california-quail: The California quails distinctive head plume curves forward like a question mark.
entries.rockhopper-penguin: Rockhopper penguins bounce from rock to rock using both feet rather than waddling.
entries.little-blue-penguin: Little blue penguins are the smallest penguin species, standing only about 13 inches tall.
entries.gentoo-penguin: Gentoo penguins are the fastest underwater swimming birds, reaching speeds of 22 mph.
entries.african-penguin: African penguins are sometimes called jackass penguins because they bray like donkeys.
entries.brown-kiwi: Kiwi eggs are enormous relative to body size, up to 20% of the females body weight.
entries.lyrebird: The lyrebird can mimic virtually any sound, including chainsaws, camera shutters, and car alarms.
entries.cassowary: The southern cassowary is considered the worlds most dangerous bird due to its powerful kicks.
entries.scarlet-macaw: Scarlet macaws can live over 75 years in captivity and mate for life.
entries.blue-and-yellow-macaw: Blue-and-yellow macaws can fly at speeds up to 35 mph and use their powerful beaks to crack hard nuts.
entries.hyacinth-macaw: The hyacinth macaw is the largest flying parrot in the world, with a wingspan over 4 feet.
entries.african-grey-parrot: African grey parrots are considered the most intelligent bird species, with cognitive abilities rivaling those of young children.
entries.budgerigar: Budgerigars are the third most popular pet in the world after dogs and cats.
entries.cockatiel: Cockatiels are one of the few parrot species that can whistle tunes accurately.
entries.keel-billed-toucan: The toucans colorful bill is surprisingly lightweight, made mostly of keratin with a honeycomb structure.
entries.toco-toucan: The toco toucans bill contains a network of blood vessels that help regulate body temperature.
entries.great-hornbill: Great hornbill pairs seal the female inside a tree cavity during nesting, leaving only a small slit for feeding.
entries.rhinoceros-hornbill: The rhinoceros hornbills upward-curved casque can grow up to 7 inches long.
entries.laughing-kookaburra: The laughing kookaburras call sounds exactly like echoing human laughter.
entries.pied-kingfisher: The pied kingfisher is the only kingfisher species that can hover over water before diving.
entries.atlantic-puffin: Puffins can carry 10 or more fish in their beaks at once thanks to specialized tongue and bill structures.
entries.tufted-puffin: Tufted puffins can dive to depths of over 200 feet to catch fish.
entries.wandering-albatross: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of any living bird, reaching over 11 feet.
entries.black-browed-albatross: Black-browed albatrosses can sleep while flying over the ocean.
entries.laysan-albatross: The oldest known wild bird in the world is a Laysan albatross named Wisdom, over 70 years old.
entries.brown-pelican: Brown pelicans can dive from heights of over 60 feet to catch fish, with air sacs cushioning the impact.
entries.american-white-pelican: American white pelicans fish cooperatively, herding schools of fish into shallow water.
entries.frigatebird: Frigatebirds can stay airborne for weeks and sleep while flying over the ocean.
entries.northern-gannet: Northern gannets plunge-dive from heights of 130 feet, hitting the water at 60 mph.
entries.blue-footed-booby: Male blue-footed boobies perform an elaborate dance, lifting their bright blue feet alternately to attract mates.
entries.red-footed-booby: Red-footed boobies are the most abundant booby species and the only ones that regularly nest in trees.
entries.great-cormorant: Cormorants have less preen oil than other waterbirds, which helps them dive but requires wing-drying.
entries.common-loon: Common loons have solid bones that make them less buoyant and better at diving than most birds.
entries.arctic-tern: Arctic terns migrate from Arctic to Antarctic and back each year, the longest migration of any animal, up to 44,000 miles.
entries.caspian-tern: The Caspian tern is the largest tern species in the world.
entries.black-skimmer: The black skimmers lower bill is longer than its upper, allowing it to skim fish from the water surface.
entries.herring-gull: Herring gulls can drink saltwater thanks to special glands above their eyes that filter out excess salt.
entries.laughing-gull: Laughing gulls are named for their call that sounds like high-pitched human laughter.
entries.killdeer: Killdeer perform a broken-wing act to lure predators away from their ground nests.
entries.american-woodcock: American woodcocks have eyes on the sides of their heads and can see 360 degrees.
entries.red-knot: Red knots migrate up to 9,000 miles nonstop from the Arctic to the tip of South America.
entries.american-avocet: American avocets sweep their upturned bills side to side through water to catch tiny invertebrates.
entries.black-necked-stilt: The black-necked stilt has the second-longest legs relative to body size of any bird, after the flamingo.
entries.willow-ptarmigan: Willow ptarmigan change color with the seasons, brown in summer and pure white in winter.
entries.spruce-grouse: Spruce grouse are so tame they are sometimes called fool hens because they rarely fly from danger.
entries.ruffed-grouse: Male ruffed grouse create a drumming sound by beating their wings rapidly to attract females.
entries.chukar: Chukars prefer running uphill to flying when escaping danger.
entries.common-crane: Common cranes perform elaborate dances with jumping, bowing, and wing-flapping during courtship.
entries.demoiselle-crane: Demoiselle cranes fly at altitudes over 26,000 feet during their Himalayan migration.
entries.bearded-vulture: Bearded vultures eat bones, dropping them from great heights to crack them into swallowable pieces.
entries.andean-condor: The Andean condor has the largest wingspan of any raptor, reaching over 10 feet.
entries.king-vulture: King vultures were believed by the Maya to carry messages between humans and gods.
entries.turkey-vulture: Turkey vultures have the best sense of smell of any bird, able to detect carrion from miles away.
entries.american-kestrel: American kestrels can see ultraviolet light, which helps them track the urine trails of rodents.
entries.merlin: Merlins were once known as pigeon hawks due to their habit of hunting pigeons.
entries.prairie-falcon: Prairie falcons can reach speeds over 45 mph in level flight and much faster in a stoop.
entries.gyrfalcon: The gyrfalcon is the largest falcon in the world and was once reserved as a bird of kings.
entries.osprey: Ospreys have reversible outer toes that allow them to grasp fish with two toes in front and two behind.
entries.northern-harrier: Northern harriers have facial discs similar to owls that help them locate prey by sound.
entries.coopers-hawk: Coopers hawks are agile enough to chase prey through dense forest at high speed.
entries.sharp-shinned-hawk: The sharp-shinned hawk is the smallest hawk in North America, barely larger than a jay.
entries.swainsons-hawk: Swainsons hawks migrate in massive flocks of hundreds of thousands from North America to South America.
entries.rough-legged-hawk: Rough-legged hawks have feathered legs all the way to their toes, adapted for Arctic cold.
entries.ferruginous-hawk: The ferruginous hawk is the largest North American hawk, with a wingspan over 5 feet.
entries.white-tailed-kite: White-tailed kites can hover in place for extended periods while scanning the ground for prey.
entries.mississippi-kite: Mississippi kites eat enormous quantities of cicadas and other insects caught in mid-air.
entries.red-winged-blackbird: Red-winged blackbirds are one of the most abundant birds in North America, with over 200 million individuals.
entries.brown-headed-cowbird: Brown-headed cowbirds are brood parasites that lay their eggs in other birds nests.
entries.common-grackle: Common grackles have iridescent feathers that shimmer purple, green, and bronze in the sunlight.
entries.great-tailed-grackle: Male great-tailed grackles have a wingspan of nearly 18 inches and their long tails make up half their total length.
entries.yellow-headed-blackbird: Male yellow-headed blackbirds defend small nesting territories within marshes, sometimes with multiple females.
entries.eastern-meadowlark: The eastern meadowlark looks almost identical to the western meadowlark but has a completely different song.
entries.western-meadowlark: The western meadowlark is the state bird of six different U.S. states, more than any other bird.
entries.orchard-oriole: The orchard oriole is the smallest icterid in North America, smaller than even the house finch.
entries.bullocks-oriole: Bullocks orioles weave elaborate hanging pouch nests that dangle from tree branches.
entries.barn-swallow: Barn swallows migrate up to 6,000 miles between their breeding and wintering grounds.
entries.tree-swallow: Tree swallows are one of the few North American songbirds that can digest berries, allowing them to migrate earlier in spring.
entries.cliff-swallow: Cliff swallows build gourd-shaped mud nests in colonies that can number in the hundreds.
entries.purple-martin: Purple martins are almost completely dependent on human-provided nest boxes in the eastern United States.
entries.bank-swallow: Bank swallows are the smallest swallow species in North America and nest in burrows dug into sandy banks.
entries.violet-green-swallow: Violet-green swallows have white patches on their face that wrap around to the back of their head.
entries.chimney-swift: Chimney swifts can spend almost their entire lives in the air, even sleeping while flying.
entries.common-nighthawk: Common nighthawks have tiny feathers around their mouth that form a wide funnel for catching insects in flight.
entries.eastern-whip-poor-will: Eastern whip-poor-wills can sing up to 400 times per hour, repeating their name-like call all night.
entries.greater-roadrunner: Greater roadrunners can run at speeds up to 20 mph and can live without drinking water.
entries.yellow-billed-cuckoo: Yellow-billed cuckoos are sometimes called rain crows because they call more frequently before storms.
entries.hoopoe: The hoopoe has a spectacular fan-like crest that it raises when excited or alarmed.
entries.tawny-frogmouth: Tawny frogmouths are often mistaken for owls but are actually more closely related to nightjars.
entries.common-potoo: Common potoos perch upright on branches during the day, looking exactly like a broken tree stump.
entries.american-goldfinch: American goldfinches are one of the latest nesting birds, often not breeding until late July.
entries.pine-grosbeak: Pine grosbeaks are one of the tamest boreal birds, often allowing close approach.
entries.evening-grosbeak: Evening grosbeaks are irruptive migrants, showing up in large numbers far south of their normal range in some years.
entries.cassins-finch: Cassins finches are the most recently described North American bird species, not recognized until 1861.
entries.red-crossbill: Red crossbills have uniquely crossed mandibles specifically adapted for extracting seeds from conifer cones.
entries.pine-siskin: Pine siskins can carry salmonella bacteria without getting sick, which can be transmitted to backyard birds at feeders.
entries.common-redpoll: Common redpolls can survive temperatures of -60 degrees Fahrenheit by eating seeds and fluffing their feathers.
entries.hoary-redpoll: The hoary redpoll is one of the hardiest songbirds, living further north than almost any other passerine.
entries.house-finch: Male house finches get their red color from pigments in their diet of berries and fruits.
entries.purple-finch: Roger Tory Peterson described male purple finches as dipped in raspberry juice.
entries.eastern-wood-pewee: The eastern wood-pewees call is so distinctive that the species was named after its song.
entries.great-crested-flycatcher: Great crested flycatchers always incorporate snakeskin into their nest material.
entries.eastern-kingbird: Eastern kingbirds are named for their aggressive territorial behavior, attacking birds much larger than themselves.
entries.eastern-phoebe: The eastern phoebe was the first bird ever banded in North America, by Audubon in 1840.
entries.willow-flycatcher: Willow flycatchers are virtually identical to several other Empidonax flycatchers and are best identified by their distinctive FITZ-bew song.
entries.scissor-tailed-flycatcher: The scissor-tailed flycatchers long tail feathers can be twice as long as its body.
entries.vermilion-flycatcher: The vermilion flycatcher is one of the most brilliantly colored flycatchers in the Western Hemisphere.
entries.common-merganser: Common mergansers have serrated bills that help them grip slippery fish while diving underwater.
entries.hooded-merganser: Hooded mergansers have the largest crest relative to body size of any duck, which they raise and lower at will.
entries.bufflehead: Buffleheads are the smallest diving ducks in North America and often nest in old woodpecker holes.
entries.common-goldeneye: Common goldeneye hens巢巢内产卵后，雌鸟会用自己腹部脱落的绒羽覆盖卵。
entries.ring-necked-duck: Despite its name, the ring-necked duck neck ring is rarely visible in the field.
entries.gadwall: The gadwall is often called the plain duck, but males have an elegant pattern of fine vermiculation visible up close.
entries.blue-winged-teal: Blue-winged teal are among the earliest spring migrants and latest fall migrants in North America.
entries.crested-caracara: Crested caracaras are members of the falcon family but behave more like vultures, often scavenging on carrion.
entries.palm-nut-vulture: The palm-nut vulture is the only vulture species that feeds primarily on plant material, specifically palm fruits.
entries.black-vulture: Black vultures have excellent eyesight and also use their sense of smell to locate carrion.
entries.roseate-spoonbill: Roseate spoonbills sweep their spatulate bills side to side through shallow water to catch small fish and crustaceans.
entries.wood-stork: Wood storks are the only stork species that breeds in North America and use tactile feeding to catch prey.
entries.white-ibis: White ibises probe mud with their long, curved bills and can detect prey by touch alone.
entries.limpkin: Limpkins are specialized apple snail eaters, with bills specifically adapted to extract snails from their shells.
entries.rusty-blackbird: The rusty blackbird has declined by over 90% in the past 50 years, making it one of North Americas fastest declining birds.
entries.blue-tang: Blue tangs can make themselves nearly invisible at night by changing color.
entries.mandarinfish: Mandarinfish are one of only two vertebrates known to produce blue pigment.
entries.sixbar-wrasse: Sixbar wrasses can change sex from female to male during their lifetime.
entries.yellowtail-coris: Juvenile yellowtail coris look completely different from adults with orange and white spotting.
entries.bicolor-angelfish: Bicolor angelfish can make loud popping sounds for communication.
entries.flame-angelfish: Flame angelfish can become aggressive when kept in small aquariums.
entries.queen-angelfish: Queen angelfish get their name from a dark blue ring on their forehead resembling a crown.
entries.french-angelfish: French angelfish are often seen in monogamous pairs and travel together for life.
entries.regal-tang: Regal tangs have a retractable spine near their tail that can inflict painful wounds.
entries.sohal-surgeonfish: Sohal surgeonfish are extremely territorial and will attack divers who enter their space.
entries.moorish-idol: Moorish idols are notoriously difficult to keep in captivity and rarely survive long in aquariums.
entries.royal-gramma: Royal grammas often hang upside down under rock ledges.
entries.longnose-butterflyfish: The longnose butterflyfish uses its elongated snout to reach into coral crevices for food.
entries.copperband-butterflyfish: Copperband butterflyfish have a false eye spot near their tail to confuse predators.
entries.foureye-butterflyfish: Foureye butterflyfish have large eye spots that make predators think their tail is their head.
entries.bluegill: Male bluegills build circular nests in shallow water and guard the eggs fiercely.
entries.largemouth-bass: Largemouth bass can open their mouths wide enough to gulp down prey nearly half their size.
entries.smallmouth-bass: Smallmouth bass are known for their fighting ability and are called brownies or bronzebacks.
entries.rainbow-trout: Rainbow trout can change color intensity based on their environment and mood.
entries.brook-trout: Brook trout are the only trout native to much of eastern North America.
entries.atlantic-salmon: Atlantic salmon can jump waterfalls and dams during their upstream spawning migration.
entries.chinook-salmon: Chinook salmon are the largest of all Pacific salmon species.
entries.coho-salmon: Coho salmon turn bright red with hooked jaws during spawning season.
entries.pacific-bluefin-tuna: Pacific bluefin tuna can cross the entire Pacific Ocean in less than 60 days.
entries.yellowfin-tuna: Yellowfin tuna can swim at speeds up to 40 miles per hour in short bursts.
entries.atlantic-cod: Atlantic cod can detect their prey using electroreception even in murky water.
entries.atlantic-grouper: Groupers can inhale prey whole by suddenly opening their massive mouths.
entries.goliath-grouper: Goliath groupers are so large they can weigh as much as a small car.
entries.red-snapper: Red snappers can live over 50 years, making them one of the longest-lived snapper species.
entries.mahi-mahi: Mahi-mahi are also called dorado or dolphinfish, not to be confused with dolphins.
entries.wahoo: Wahoo are among the fastest fish in the ocean, capable of reaching speeds up to 50 mph.
entries.sailfish: Sailfish are considered the fastest fish in the ocean, reaching speeds up to 68 mph.
entries.blue-marlin: Blue marlin can weigh over 1,000 pounds and are among the largest bony fish in the world.
entries.nassau-grouper: Nassau grouper can change color in seconds to match their surroundings.
entries.striped-bass: Striped bass are anadromous and can travel hundreds of miles to spawn.
entries.red-drum: Red drum are also called channel bass and are the official state fish of North Carolina.
entries.black-drum: Black drum can produce loud drumming sounds using muscles on their swim bladder.
entries.channel-catfish: Channel catfish have taste buds covering their entire body and can taste food from far away.
entries.blue-catfish: Blue catfish can grow over 100 pounds and are the largest freshwater fish in North America.
entries.walking-catfish: Walking catfish can survive out of water for hours and use their pectoral fins to walk on land.
entries.wels-catfish: Wels catfish have been reported to grow over 16 feet long in rare cases.
entries.eurasian-pike: Eurasian pike can accelerate from a standstill to 20 mph in less than a tenth of a second.
entries.muskellunge: Muskellunge are also called muskies and are the largest member of the pike family.
entries.walleye: Walleye have a light-reflecting layer called the tapetum lucidum that makes their eyes glow at night.
entries.common-carp: Common carp are considered one of the most influential invasive fish species in the world.
entries.grass-carp: Grass carp can eat up to 40% of their body weight in vegetation each day.
entries.koi-carp: The most expensive koi ever sold was a Japanese fish named S Legend that sold for $1.8 million.
entries.tench: Tench secrete a mucus that can heal wounds in other fish.
entries.three-spined-stickleback: Male sticklebacks build elaborate nests from water plants and fan the eggs to provide oxygen.
entries.florida-gar: Florida gar have an elongated snout filled with needle-like teeth and can breathe air.
entries.alligator-gar: Alligator gar eggs are toxic to humans but consumed by Native Americans after processing.
entries.bowfin: Bowfin are the only surviving member of an ancient order of fish.
entries.chinese-sturgeon: Chinese sturgeon have existed for over 140 million years and are called living fossils.
entries.atlantic-sturgeon: Atlantic sturgeon can live over 100 years and were once hunted for their caviar.
entries.arctic-char: Arctic char are the most northerly freshwater fish in the world.
entries.lake-trout: Lake trout can live over 40 years and grow to over 60 pounds.
entries.cutthroat-trout: Cutthroat trout are named for the distinctive red slash under their jaw.
entries.golden-trout: Golden trout are the official state fish of California and are found only in a few remote streams.
entries.oceanic-whitetip-shark: Oceanic whitetip sharks were responsible for more human casualties than any other species during World War II.
entries.blacktip-shark: Blacktip sharks are known for their dramatic breaching behavior, spinning out of the water.
entries.scalloped-hammerhead: Scalloped hammerheads form massive schools of hundreds during their annual migration.
entries.thresher-shark: Thresher sharks use their extremely long tail whip to stun schools of fish.
entries.basking-shark: Basking sharks are the second largest fish in the world, after whale sharks.
entries.nurse-shark: Nurse sharks can pump water over their gills while resting on the ocean floor.
entries.zebra-shark: Zebra sharks change from striped as juveniles to spotted as adults.
entries.epaulette-shark: Epaulette sharks can walk on their fins across the reef flat at low tide.
entries.angel-shark: Angel sharks can bury themselves completely in sand to ambush passing prey.
entries.southern-stingray: Southern stingrays can deliver a venomous barb sting that can cause severe pain.
entries.cownose-ray: Cownose rays migrate in massive schools of thousands along the Atlantic coast.
entries.eagle-ray: Spotted eagle rays can leap several feet out of the water.
entries.viperfish: Viperfish have extremely long, needle-like teeth that are so long they don't fit inside their mouths.
entries.gulper-eel: Gulper eels have enormous mouths that can open wide enough to swallow prey larger than themselves.
entries.lungfish: Lungfish can breathe air and survive out of water for months by burrowing into mud.
entries.coelacanth: Coelacanths were thought to be extinct for 66 million years until rediscovered in 1938.
entries.red-bellied-piranha: Red-bellied piranhas can strip a carcass to bone in minutes with their razor-sharp teeth.
entries.arapaima: Arapaima are among the largest freshwater fish in the world and can breathe air.
entries.arowana: Arowana can jump up to 6 feet out of the water to catch prey on overhanging branches.
entries.knifefish: Black ghost knifefish use weak electric fields to navigate and find prey in dark, murky water.
entries.betta: Male bettas build bubble nests at the water surface for their eggs.
entries.discus: Discus parents produce a mucus secretion that their young feed on for the first few weeks.
entries.oscarr: Oscars are highly intelligent fish that can recognize their owners.
entries.angelfish-freshwater: Freshwater angelfish are actually cichlids, not related to marine angelfish.
entries.convict-cichlid: Convict cichlids are devoted parents that aggressively defend their young.
entries.peacock-cichlid: Male peacock cichlids display brilliant blue, red, and gold colors during breeding.
entries.lionfish: Lionfish venomous spines can cause extreme pain and their venom is heat-stable.
entries.stonefish: Stonefish are the most venomous fish in the world, their sting can be fatal to humans.
entries.leafy-seadragon: Leafy seadragons have no stomach or teeth and must eat almost constantly.
entries.weedy-seadragon: Weedy seadragons carry their eggs on the male's tail until they hatch.
entries.boxfish: Boxfish can release a toxin when stressed that can kill other fish in an aquarium.
entries.cowfish: Longhorn cowfish have two horn-like spines protruding from their head.
entries.trunkfish: Trunkfish can squirt a toxic substance from their skin when threatened.
entries.filefish: Filefish can change color and pattern to match their surroundings.
entries.triggerfish: Triggerfish have a spine on their dorsal fin that can be locked in an upright position.
entries.leatherjacket: Leatherjackets have rough, sandpaper-like skin used by early settlers as sandpaper.
entries.parrotfish: Parrotfish excrete digested coral as fine white sand, creating tropical beaches.
entries.wrasse: Cleaner wrasses set up cleaning stations where larger fish line up to have parasites removed.
entries.tuskfish: Tuskfish use rocks as anvils to crack open shellfish for food.
entries.grouper-marbled: Marbled groupers form massive spawning aggregations of thousands of individuals.
entries.wrasse-humphead: Humphead wrasses can live over 30 years and are the largest living labrid fish.
entries.coral-grouper: Coral groupers hunt cooperatively with moray eels, using head shakes to signal the eel to flush out prey.
entries.cardinalfish: Male Banggai cardinalfish mouthbrood the eggs until they hatch.
entries.damselfish: Male garibaldi build and tend elaborate nests of algae to attract mates.
entries.sergeant-major: Male sergeant majors turn dark purple when guarding their eggs.
entries.goby: Neon gobies set up cleaning stations and remove parasites from larger fish.
entries.blenny: Midas blennies often join schools of cleaner wrasses to avoid predation.
entries.scorpionfish: Scorpionfish are masters of camouflage, resembling algae-covered rocks on the reef.
entries.flathead: Flathead are ambush predators that bury themselves in sand to surprise prey.
entries.grunt: Grunts get their name from the sound they make by grinding their teeth.
entries.tang: Clown tangs are extremely territorial and can be aggressive toward other fish.
entries.squirrelfish: Squirrelfish have large eyes adapted for nocturnal hunting.
entries.sweep: Sweep are named for their distinctive sweeping swimming motion.
entries.leatherjacket-freshwater: New Zealand magpie are freshwater leatherjackets found only in New Zealand.
entries.john-dory: John Dory have a distinctive dark spot on each side that looks like a thumbprint.
entries.boarfish: Boarfish use their elongated snout to extract small invertebrates from coral crevices.
entries.bigeye: Bigeyes have extremely large eyes adapted for nocturnal feeding.
entries.soldierfish: Soldierfish are nocturnal and hide in reef crevices during the day.
entries.green-anole: Green anoles can change color from bright green to brown based on mood, temperature, or social signals.
entries.saltwater-crocodile: Saltwater crocodiles have the strongest bite force of any living animal, estimated at over 3700 psi.
entries.reticulated-python: The reticulated python is the longest snake in the world, with some individuals exceeding 23 feet.
entries.panther-chameleon: Chameleons change color primarily for communication and temperature regulation, not camouflage.
entries.american-alligator: American alligators can regulate their body temperature by opening their mouths to cool down, known as gaping.
entries.leopard-gecko: Leopard geckos can store fat in their tails, which can detach if grabbed by a predator and later regrow.
entries.eastern-diamondback-rattlesnake: The eastern diamondback rattlesnake's rattle can vibrate up to 50 times per second as a warning signal.
entries.gila-monster: The Gila monster's venom contains a compound used in a drug to treat type 2 diabetes.
entries.leatherback-sea-turtle: Leatherback sea turtles are the largest turtles in the world and have existed for over 100 million years.
entries.boomslang: Boomslang venom prevents blood clotting, causing victims to bleed from every orifice.
entries.indian-cobra: The Indian cobra's iconic hood markings are thought to resemble eyes, deterring predators from attacking from behind.
entries.rhinoceros-iguana: Rhinoceros iguanas get their name from the horn-like scales on their snouts, which resemble rhinoceros horns.
entries.emerald-tree-boa: Emerald tree boas have heat-sensing pits along their lips to detect warm-blooded prey in the dark.
entries.gharial: Gharials have the longest and thinnest snouts of any crocodilian, perfectly shaped for catching fish.
entries.mexican-beaded-lizard: The Mexican beaded lizard is one of only a few venomous lizards and can deliver a painful, though rarely fatal, bite.
entries.desert-tortoise: Desert tortoises can store over a liter of water in their bladders and reabsorb it during droughts.
entries.tokay-gecko: Tokay geckos can produce one of the loudest calls of any gecko, heard up to a mile away.
entries.king-snake: King snakes are called 'kings' because they regularly eat other snakes, including venomous rattlesnakes.
entries.blue-tongued-skink: Blue-tongued skinks flash their bright blue tongues to startle predators into backing away.
entries.american-crocodile: American crocodiles are more tolerant of saltwater than alligators, which is why they are found in coastal habitats.
entries.asian-water-monitor: Asian water monitors are excellent swimmers and can hold their breath for up to 30 minutes.
entries.eastern-hognose-snake: Hognose snakes are famous for playing dead when threatened, rolling onto their backs with their mouths open.
entries.sailfin-lizard: Sailfin lizards can run across the surface of water for short distances using their flattened, fringed toes.
entries.texas-rat-snake: Texas rat snakes are excellent climbers and have been found in trees more than 40 feet high.
entries.gopher-tortoise: Gopher tortoise burrows can be over 40 feet long and provide shelter for more than 350 other species.
entries.bush-viper: Bush vipers have keeled, leaf-like scales that give them a spiky, dragon-like appearance unique among snakes.
entries.pancake-tortoise: Pancake tortoises have flat, flexible shells that allow them to wedge themselves into rock crevices to escape predators.
entries.cottonmouth: Cottonmouths get their name from the white, cotton-like lining of their mouth, which they display as a warning.
entries.cuban-crocodile: Cuban crocodiles are the most terrestrial of the New World crocodiles and can gallop like a horse.
entries.bearded-dragon: Bearded dragons puff out their spiny throat scales and open their mouths to appear larger when threatened.
entries.yellow-bellied-slider: Yellow-bellied sliders can bask on logs for hours, using the sun to regulate their body temperature and digest food.
entries.western-diamondback-rattlesnake: Western diamondback rattlesnakes add a new segment to their rattle each time they shed their skin.
entries.caiman-lizard: Caiman lizards have powerful jaws and thick, armored scales that resemble those of caiman crocodilians.
entries.nile-crocodile: Nile crocodiles are considered the most dangerous crocodile species to humans, with an estimated 1000 attacks per year.
entries.carpet-python: Carpet pythons are nocturnal hunters that use heat-sensing pits to detect warm-blooded prey in total darkness.
entries.brown-basilisk: Brown basilisks can run across water using their long toes and fringed scales, earning them the nickname 'Jesus Christ lizard'.
entries.dumerils-boa: Dumeril's boa can reduce its metabolic rate to survive extended periods without food, going months between meals.
entries.sulcata-tortoise: Sulcata tortoises dig extensive burrows up to 10 feet deep to escape the extreme heat of the African savanna.
entries.common-caiman: Common caimans have a bony ridge between their eyes that acts like a built-in pair of sunglasses in bright sunlight.
entries.western-hognose-snake: Western hognose snakes flatten their heads and hiss loudly when threatened, but their bluff rarely escalates to biting.
entries.forest-cobra: The forest cobra is the largest true cobra species and an excellent swimmer, often found near water.
entries.veiled-chameleon: Male veiled chameleons have a tall casque on their heads that may help channel dew drops into their mouths.
entries.rough-scaled-sand-boa: Sand boas spend most of their lives buried underground, with only their eyes and snout visible above the sand.
entries.philippine-crocodile: The Philippine crocodile is the most endangered crocodilian in the world, with fewer than 100 left in the wild.
entries.rainbow-boa: Rainbow boas have iridescent scales that refract light, creating a stunning rainbow shimmer in the sun.
entries.giant-plated-lizard: Giant plated lizards wedge themselves into rock crevices and inflate their bodies, making them nearly impossible to extract.
entries.black-spiny-tailed-iguana: The black spiny-tailed iguana is the fastest lizard in the world, capable of running at 21 mph.
entries.burmese-python: Burmese pythons are one of the largest snake species and have become a destructive invasive species in the Florida Everglades.
entries.ornate-box-turtle: Ornate box turtles can completely seal their hinged plastron shut, trapping themselves inside their shell for protection.
entries.common-house-gecko: Common house geckos are one of the most widespread lizard species on Earth, found on every continent except Antarctica.
entries.sidewinder-rattlesnake: Sidewinders move using a unique S-shaped locomotion that minimizes contact with hot desert sand.
entries.chinese-water-dragon: Chinese water dragons can drop from heights of 40 feet and land safely on branches below.
entries.west-african-dwarf-crocodile: West African dwarf crocodiles are the most terrestrial of all crocodilians and dig deep burrows to rest in during the day.
entries.cape-cobra: Cape cobras are highly venomous and are responsible for the most snakebite deaths in southern Africa.
entries.crested-iguana: Crested iguanas can change color from green to black based on temperature and social context.
entries.argentine-tegu: Argentine tegus can regulate their body temperature during the reproductive season without relying solely on external heat.
entries.king-brown-snake: The king brown snake is technically a black snake, not a brown snake, and is in the genus Pseudechis.
entries.false-gharial: The false gharial has a narrow snout similar to the true gharial but is not closely related to it.
entries.indian-star-tortoise: Indian star tortoises have star-shaped patterns on their shells that help with camouflage and thermoregulation.
entries.green-anaconda: The green anaconda is the heaviest snake in the world, with some individuals weighing over 220 pounds.
entries.tuatara: Tuatara are the last surviving members of an order of reptiles that lived alongside dinosaurs over 200 million years ago.
entries.eastern-water-dragon: Eastern water dragons can swim underwater for up to 90 minutes, closing a special membrane to keep water out of their eyes.
entries.spider-tortoise: Spider tortoises are named for the radiating yellow lines on their shells that resemble a spider's web.
entries.russian-tortoise: Russian tortoises can survive extreme temperatures by brumating underground for up to 6 months during harsh winters.
entries.cat-eyed-snake: Cat-eyed snakes have vertical pupils like cats, giving them excellent night vision for hunting in the dark rainforest.
entries.arabian-chameleon: Arabian chameleons are one of the few chameleon species adapted to live in hot, arid desert conditions.
entries.spotted-turtle: Spotted turtles have yellow spots on their dark shells that become more numerous with age, like counting tree rings.
entries.banded-krait: Banded kraits are twice as venomous as cobras and often cannibalize other snakes, including other kraits.
entries.golden-skink: Golden skinks have a metallic, iridescent sheen that makes them look like they are coated in gold.
entries.broad-snouted-caiman: Broad-snouted caimans build mounds of vegetation to incubate their eggs, using decomposition heat to warm them.
entries.copperhead: Copperheads account for the majority of venomous snakebites in the United States, though their venom is rarely fatal.
entries.radiated-tortoise: Radiated tortoises can live for over 100 years, with some individuals reportedly reaching 188 years of age.
entries.blue-racer: Blue racers are one of the fastest snakes in North America, capable of speeds up to 10 mph.
entries.side-blotched-lizard: Male side-blotched lizards use a rock-paper-scissors strategy with three throat colors to compete for mates.
entries.nile-monitor: Nile monitors are excellent swimmers and can hold their breath for up to an hour while submerged underwater.
entries.canebrake-rattlesnake: Canebrake rattlesnakes have a silent rattle compared to other rattlesnake species, often delivering strikes without warning.
entries.yellow-footed-tortoise: Yellow-footed tortoises play a crucial role in seed dispersal in the Amazon, helping to regenerate the rainforest.
entries.puff-adder: Puff adders are responsible for more snakebite deaths in Africa than any other snake due to their excellent camouflage.
entries.eastern-green-mamba: Eastern green mambas are arboreal and rarely descend to the ground, spending their lives in the forest canopy.
entries.cape-dwarf-chameleon: Cape dwarf chameleons have independently moving eyes that can rotate 180 degrees, giving them a 360-degree field of vision.
entries.chinese-alligator: Chinese alligators are the most endangered crocodilian species, with fewer than 150 individuals remaining in the wild.
entries.snouted-cobra: Snouted cobras can spit venom accurately up to 2 meters, aiming for the eyes of perceived threats.
entries.common-wall-lizard: Common wall lizards have been introduced to North America from Europe and are now thriving in cities like Toronto and Vancouver.
entries.brown-tree-snake: The brown tree snake has driven at least 10 bird species to extinction on Guam after accidentally introduced there.
entries.angulate-tortoise: Angulate tortoises are the most southerly distributed tortoise species in Africa, found even in the cool, wet Western Cape.
entries.savannah-monitor: Savannah monitors can slow their metabolism so much that they can survive on as few as three large meals per year.
entries.white-lipped-pit-viper: White-lipped pit vipers have heat-sensing pits between their eyes and nostrils that detect warm-blooded prey in complete darkness.
entries.alabama-red-bellied-cooter: Alabama red-bellied cooters can bask for hours, using the sun to synthesize vitamin D3 for shell health.
entries.amazon-tree-boa: Amazon tree boas are incredibly variable in color and pattern, with no two individuals looking exactly alike.
entries.california-kingsnake: California kingsnakes are immune to rattlesnake venom and regularly prey upon rattlesnakes in the wild.
entries.clouded-monitor: Clouded monitors are arboreal and have sharp claws that allow them to climb vertical tree trunks with ease.
entries.brazilian-rainbow-boa: Brazilian rainbow boas have iridescent scales that create a holographic rainbow effect when exposed to light.
entries.northern-cuirassated-lizard: Northern cuirassated lizards have bony armor plates called osteoderms that provide protection from predators.
entries.desert-iguana: Desert iguanas can tolerate body temperatures up to 120°F, making them one of the most heat-tolerant lizards.
entries.false-water-cobra: False water cobras flatten their necks like true cobras when threatened, despite being only mildly venomous.
entries.garter-snake: Garter snakes are mildly venomous but harmless to humans, making them one of the most common backyard snakes.
entries.shingleback-skink: Shingleback skinks mate for life and reunite with the same partner every breeding season.
entries.mozambique-spitting-cobra: Mozambique spitting cobras can spit venom accurately up to 3 meters, targeting the eyes of threats.
entries.american-bullfrog: American Bullfrogs can eat almost anything they can fit in their mouths, including other frogs, birds, and even snakes.
entries.glass-frog: Glass Frogs have transparent abdominal skin that allows you to see their beating heart and internal organs.
entries.pacman-frog: Pacman Frogs are named after the video game character due to their enormous mouths and round bodies.
entries.budgetts-frog: Budgett's Frogs inflate their bodies and scream when threatened to appear larger and more intimidating.
entries.whites-tree-frog: White's Tree Frogs have fatty deposits above their eyes that look like eyebrows, giving them a perpetual smile.
entries.african-dwarf-frog: African Dwarf Frogs are fully aquatic and spend their entire lives underwater, unlike most frogs.
entries.amazon-milk-frog: Amazon Milk Frogs secrete a milky white toxin when threatened and can change color from light to dark blue.
entries.gray-tree-frog: Gray Tree Frogs can change color from gray to green depending on their environment and activity level.
entries.spring-peeper: The Spring Peeper's high-pitched peeping call can be heard from over a mile away during breeding season.
entries.wood-frog: Wood Frogs can survive being frozen solid, with up to 65% of their body water turning to ice.
entries.american-toad: A single American Toad can eat up to 1,000 insects per day, making them excellent garden pest controllers.
entries.cane-toad: Cane Toads were introduced to Australia in 1935 to control beetles but became one of the worst invasive species in the world.
entries.fire-bellied-toad: Fire-Bellied Toads display their bright orange-red bellies when threatened in a behavior called the unken reflex.
entries.desert-rain-frog: Desert Rain Frogs let out a high-pitched squeak when threatened, sounding like a dog toy.
entries.goliath-frog: The Goliath Frog is the largest living frog in the world, weighing up to 7 pounds and spanning over a foot long.
entries.mountain-chicken-frog: Despite their name, Mountain Chicken Frogs are not chickens but are called so because their leg meat tastes like chicken.
entries.spadefoot-toad: Spadefoot Toads can burrow underground and remain dormant for up to nine months, emerging only when it rains.
entries.natterjack-toad: Natterjack Toads are one of the loudest European amphibians, with calls that can be heard over a mile away.
entries.midwife-toad: Male Midwife Toads carry the eggs wrapped around their hind legs until they are ready to hatch.
entries.european-tree-frog: European Tree Frogs have adhesive toe pads that allow them to climb smooth surfaces, including glass.
entries.leopard-frog: Leopard Frogs can jump up to 20 times their body length in a single leap.
entries.strawberry-poison-dart-frog: The Strawberry Poison Dart Frog has over 30 color morphs, ranging from red with blue legs to green with yellow spots.
entries.dyeing-poison-dart-frog: The Dyeing Poison Dart Frog was named because indigenous people used its toxins to dye fabric.
entries.harlequin-toad: Many Harlequin Toad species were thought to be extinct until small populations were rediscovered in recent years.
entries.pickerel-frog: Pickerel Frogs produce a toxin that can irritate human skin and is lethal to other frogs.
entries.cherry-tree-frog: Cherry Tree Frogs can change color from bright green to brown depending on their surroundings.
entries.asian-common-toad: Asian Common Toads are extremely adaptable and thrive in human-modified environments across Southeast Asia.
entries.clown-tree-frog: Clown Tree Frogs are named for their playful, acrobatic movements through the trees.
entries.gliding-tree-frog: Gliding Tree Frogs can spread their enlarged toe pads and webbed feet to glide between trees.
entries.black-legged-poison-frog: Black-Legged Poison Frogs exhibit biparental care, with both parents tending to their eggs and tadpoles.
entries.red-backed-poison-frog: Red-Backed Poison Frogs use their bright coloration to warn predators of their skin toxins in a strategy called aposematism.
entries.splashback-poison-frog: Splashback Poison Frogs get their name from their colorful backs that look like paint splashes.
entries.cane-turtle-frog: Cane Turtle Frogs have a flattened body shape that allows them to hide under rocks and logs.
entries.malaysian-horned-frog: Malaysian Horned Frogs have horn-like projections above their eyes that help break up their outline among leaf litter.
entries.hampire-poison-dart-frog: Hampire Poison Dart Frogs are named after the Harry Potter character due to their striking black and orange pattern.
entries.brazilian-horned-frog: Brazilian Horned Frogs are ambush predators that can remain motionless for hours waiting for prey.
entries.hairy-frog: Male Hairy Frogs grow hair-like skin projections during breeding season to help absorb oxygen from water.
entries.tomato-frog: Tomato Frogs secrete a thick, white substance that can glue a predator's mouth shut.
entries.marsupial-frog: Female Marsupial Frogs carry their eggs in a pouch on their back, similar to marsupial mammals.
entries.foam-nest-frog: Foam Nest Frogs create a frothy nest by beating their hind legs to whip up a foam that protects their eggs.
entries.surinam-toad: Female Surinam Toads have eggs embedded in the skin of their backs, where they develop into froglets.
entries.tiger-salamander: Tiger Salamanders are one of the longest-lived amphibians, with some individuals living over 20 years in captivity.
entries.eastern-newt: The juvenile Eastern Newt, called a red eft, is brightly colored to warn predators of its toxins.
entries.hellbender: Hellbenders absorb oxygen through their wrinkly skin and are an indicator species for water quality.
entries.olm: Olms can survive without food for up to 10 years and are among the longest-lived amphibians.
entries.fire-salamander: Fire Salamanders were once believed to be born from fire and could extinguish flames with their cold bodies.
entries.spotted-salamander: Spotted Salamanders have a symbiotic relationship with algae that lives inside their cells.
entries.red-backed-salamander: Red-Backed Salamanders breathe entirely through their skin and have no lungs or gills as adults.
entries.mudpuppy: Mudpuppies retain their external gills throughout their entire lives, a condition called neoteny.
entries.rough-skinned-newt: Rough-Skinned Newts produce enough tetrodotoxin to kill several adult humans.
entries.alpine-salamander: Alpine Salamanders are entirely viviparous, giving birth to fully developed young rather than laying eggs.
entries.great-crested-newt: Male Great Crested Newts develop a jagged crest along their back during breeding season.
entries.marbled-salamander: Female Marbled Salamanders stay with their eggs and guard them until they hatch.
entries.long-toed-salamander: Long-Toed Salamanders can have up to 13 toes on their hind feet, more than most salamanders.
entries.slimy-salamander: Slimy Salamanders secrete a sticky, glue-like substance from their skin that is difficult to remove.
entries.red-salamander: Red Salamanders are one of the largest lungless salamanders in North America.
entries.lesser-siren: Lesser Sirens can breathe through their gills and also through their skin, and can survive drying by burrowing into mud.
entries.greater-siren: Greater Sirens are the largest species in the Sirenidae family and can exceed three feet in length.
entries.three-toed-amphiuma: Three-Toed Amphiumas have vestigial legs that are so small they are almost impossible to see.
entries.waterdog: Waterdogs retain their external gills throughout their lives, a condition known as neoteny.
entries.spring-salamander: Spring Salamanders are one of the few salamander species that can live their entire lives in water.
entries.cave-salamander: Cave Salamanders can climb vertical rock faces using their specialized toe pads.
entries.arboreal-salamander: Arboreal Salamanders can climb trees and have prehensile tails for gripping branches.
entries.ensatina: Ensatina salamanders form a ring species around California's Central Valley, with different subspecies at each end.
entries.slender-salamander: Slender Salamanders can coil into a tight spiral to conserve moisture.
entries.ringed-salamander: Ringed Salamanders migrate to breed during autumn rains, one of the few fall-breeding amphibians.
entries.flatwoods-salamander: Flatwoods Salamanders have a distinctive dark crossband pattern that helps them camouflage on the forest floor.
entries.dusky-salamander: Dusky Salamanders can autotomize their tails when threatened, which continue to wiggle and distract predators.
entries.four-toed-salamander: Four-Toed Salamanders have only four toes on their hind feet, unlike most salamanders which have five.
entries.gulf-coast-salamander: Gulf Coast Salamanders are one of the few salamander species that can tolerate slightly brackish water.
entries.tropical-caecilian: Caecilians are often mistaken for snakes or worms, but they are actually limbless amphibians.
entries.boulengers-caecilian: Boulenger's Caecilians have minute vestigial eyes that can detect light but not form images.
entries.ringed-caecilian: Ringed Caecilians have a unique sensory organ called a tentacle that helps them detect prey underground.
entries.luna-moth: Luna moths do not have mouths and cannot eat as adults, living only on stored energy.
entries.atlas-moth: The atlas moth is one of the largest insects in the world by wing area.
entries.swallowtail-butterfly: Female swallowtails can mimic the toxic pipevine swallowtail to avoid predators.
entries.hawk-moth: Hawk moths are among the fastest flying insects, capable of hovering like hummingbirds.
entries.painted-lady-butterfly: Painted ladies migrate across the Sahara Desert and the Mediterranean Sea.
entries.blue-morpho-butterfly: The morpho's blue color is not pigment but structural coloration from microscopic scales.
entries.glasswing-butterfly: The glasswing butterfly has nearly transparent wings due to nanopillar structures.
entries.cecropia-moth: The cecropia moth is the largest native moth in North America.
entries.io-moth: Each wing of the io moth has a large, striking eyespot that deters predators.
entries.polyphemus-moth: The polyphemus moth is named after the one-eyed Greek giant Polyphemus.
entries.viceroy-butterfly: Viceroys mimic the toxic monarch butterfly for protection from predators.
entries.red-admiral-butterfly: Red admirals are territorial and will chase other butterflies from their favorite basking spots.
entries.great-spangled-fritillary: Fritillary caterpillars feed exclusively on violets, which is how the group got its name.
entries.clouded-yellow-butterfly: Clouded yellows are strong migrants that can travel hundreds of miles.
entries.comma-butterfly: The comma butterfly is named for the small white comma-shaped mark on its underwings.
entries.mourning-cloak-butterfly: The mourning cloak is one of the longest-lived butterflies and overwinters as an adult.
entries.zebra-longwing-butterfly: Zebra longwings are the state butterfly of Florida and can live on pollen alone.
entries.snowflake-butterfly: The snowflake butterfly has mostly white wings with delicate black tips.
entries.resurrection-butterfly: The resurrection butterfly is considered a symbol of rebirth in Japanese culture.
entries.cabbage-white-butterfly: The small white is one of the most common butterflies in the world and a notorious garden pest.
entries.atlas-beetle: Atlas beetles can carry objects 850 times their own body weight.
entries.goliath-beetle: Goliath beetles are among the heaviest insects in the world.
entries.rhinoceros-beetle: Rhinoceros beetles can lift objects 850 times their own body weight.
entries.stag-beetle: Male stag beetles use their enormous mandibles to wrestle rivals for mates.
entries.dung-beetle: Dung beetles navigate using the Milky Way, the first insects found to use stars.
entries.tiger-beetle: Tiger beetles run so fast they go temporarily blind because their eyes cannot process images quickly enough.
entries.longhorn-beetle: The Asian longhorned beetle can kill healthy hardwood trees by tunneling through their bark.
entries.click-beetle: Click beetles can launch themselves into the air with a clicking mechanism without using their legs.
entries.bombardier-beetle: Bombardier beetles spray a boiling chemical spray at 212 degrees Fahrenheit from their abdomen.
entries.june-bug: June bugs are clumsy fliers and often bounce off windows and walls.
entries.whirligig-beetle: Whirligig beetles have four eyes: two for seeing above water and two for seeing below.
entries.diving-beetle: Diving beetles carry an air bubble under their wing covers to breathe underwater.
entries.oil-beetle: Oil beetles secrete oily droplets from their joints that repel predators and can blister human skin.
entries.bess-beetle: Bess beetles communicate by rubbing their abdomen to make squeaking sounds.
entries.bark-beetle: Mountain pine beetle outbreaks can kill millions of acres of forest in a single year.
entries.sacred-scarab-beetle: Ancient Egyptians revered the scarab as a symbol of the sun god Khepri.
entries.carrion-beetle: Carrion beetles can locate a dead animal from over a mile away using chemical sensors.
entries.patrol-bess-beetle: Patrol bess beetles produce sounds by rubbing ridges on their abdomen when disturbed.
entries.eyed-click-beetle: The eyed click beetle has two large eyespots on its thorax that startle predators.
entries.rose-chafer: Rose chafers can fly with their elytra closed, using only their hind wings.
entries.japanese-beetle: Japanese beetles release aggregation pheromones that attract more beetles to feed.
entries.colorado-potato-beetle: The Colorado potato beetle is one of the most insecticide-resistant pests in the world.
entries.lily-beetle: Lily beetles are bright red, making them easy to spot on green leaves.
entries.elm-beetle: Elm leaf beetles can enter homes through small cracks and hibernate indoors during winter.
entries.fire-ant: Fire ant colonies can form living rafts that float on water for weeks during floods.
entries.leafcutter-ant: Leafcutter ants are the largest consumers of vegetation in the Neotropics.
entries.bullet-ant: The bullet ant's sting is rated as the most painful insect sting in the world.
entries.army-ant: Army ant colonies of millions move in massive raiding columns that devour everything in their path.
entries.trap-jaw-ant: Trap-jaw ants can snap their mandibles at speeds exceeding 140 mph.
entries.weaver-ant: Weaver ants use their own larvae as living glue guns to stitch leaves together.
entries.honeybee: A single honeybee colony can visit over 225,000 flowers to produce one pound of honey.
entries.bumblebee: Bumblebees can fly in colder temperatures than most bees due to their ability to thermoregulate.
entries.carpenter-bee: Carpenter bees drill perfectly round holes in wood to create nesting galleries.
entries.paper-wasp: Paper wasps build their nests from chewed wood fibers mixed with saliva.
entries.yellow-jacket: Yellow jacket colonies can grow to contain 4,000 or more workers by late summer.
entries.bald-faced-hornet: Bald-faced hornets can spray venom from their stingers up to several feet.
entries.european-hornet: European hornets are attracted to light and will often fly into homes at night.
entries.tarantula-hawk-wasp: The tarantula hawk has one of the most painful insect stings in the world.
entries.cuckoo-wasp: Cuckoo wasps can curl into a ball when threatened, using their armored exoskeleton for protection.
entries.ichneumon-wasp: The giant ichneumon's ovipositor can be longer than its body and drills through wood to reach beetle larvae.
entries.asian-giant-hornet: The Asian giant hornet can decapitate an entire honeybee colony in hours.
entries.sweat-bee: Some sweat bees have metallic green or blue bodies that shimmer in the sunlight.
entries.mason-bee: Mason bees are 100 times more efficient at pollinating than honeybees.
entries.mining-bee: Mining bees create small volcano-shaped mounds of soil at their nest entrances.
entries.golden-digger-wasp: Golden digger wasps paralyze grasshoppers and crickets to feed their larvae alive.
entries.mud-dauber-wasp: Mud daubers stock their nests with paralyzed spiders for their developing larvae.
entries.horned-mason-bee: Male horned mason bees have small horns on their faces used in mating displays.
entries.wool-carder-bee: Wool carder bees scrape plant hairs to line their nests, hence their name.
entries.cicada-killer-wasp: The cicada killer is the largest wasp in North America and can be over 2 inches long.
entries.red-velvet-ant: The velvet ant is actually a wingless wasp with one of the most painful stings in the insect world.
entries.cuckoo-bumblebee: Cuckoo bumblebees infiltrate other bumblebee nests and lay their eggs for the host to raise.
entries.mosquito: Only female mosquitoes bite, needing blood protein to produce eggs.
entries.house-fly: House flies taste with their feet and can detect food from miles away.
entries.fruit-fly: Fruit flies are one of the most important model organisms in genetics research.
entries.crane-fly: Crane flies are often mistakenly called giant mosquitoes but do not bite or suck blood.
entries.horsefly: Horse flies are among the fastest flying insects, reaching speeds up to 90 mph.
entries.bot-fly: Bot fly larvae develop under human skin, creating painful boils called myiasis.
entries.hover-fly: Hover flies mimic bees and wasps for protection but are completely harmless.
entries.black-fly: Black fly swarms can be so dense that they suffocate livestock by blocking their airways.
entries.damselfly: Damselflies fold their wings along their bodies when at rest, unlike dragonflies.
entries.blue-dasher-dragonfly: Blue dashers can fly backwards and hover in place like a helicopter.
entries.emperor-dragonfly: Emperor dragonflies can eat their own body weight in insects every day.
entries.four-spotted-chaser: Four-spotted chasers are among the first dragonflies to emerge in spring.
entries.robber-fly: Robber flies can capture and eat insects as large as dragonflies and grasshoppers.
entries.marmalade-hoverfly: Marmalade hoverflies migrate thousands of miles across Europe each year.
entries.common-mosquito: Mosquitoes are responsible for more human deaths than any other animal in history.
entries.biting-midge: Biting midges, or no-see-ums, are so small they can pass through standard window screens.
entries.deer-fly: Deer flies are attracted to dark colors and carbon dioxide, similar to mosquitoes.
entries.cattle-bot-fly: Cattle bot fly larvae attach to the tongues and throat of cattle, causing significant irritation.
entries.orchid-mantis: The orchid mantis looks so much like a flower that pollinators land directly on it.
entries.ghost-mantis: The ghost mantis looks exactly like a dried, dead leaf, making it nearly invisible.
entries.leaf-mantis: The dead leaf mantis has irregular body edges that perfectly replicate a torn, decaying leaf.
entries.walking-stick: Walking sticks can regenerate lost limbs during molts and some species produce toxic defensive chemicals.
entries.giant-walking-stick: The giant walking stick holds the record for the longest insect in the world.
entries.american-cockroach: Cockroaches can survive for weeks without food and hold their breath for 40 minutes.
entries.german-cockroach: German cockroaches can produce up to 30,000 offspring in a single year from one female.
entries.madagascar-hissing-cockroach: Madagascar hissing cockroaches produce a loud hiss by forcing air through specialized breathing holes.
entries.oriental-cockroach: Oriental cockroaches are sometimes called water bugs because they prefer damp, dark environments.
entries.eastern-subterranean-termite: Subterranean termite colonies can contain millions of individuals working together.
entries.formosan-termite: Formosan termites build carton nests above ground and can consume a foot of 2x4 lumber in about five months.
entries.dampwood-termite: Dampwood termites are the largest North American termites and do not require soil contact.
entries.drywood-termite: Drywood termites kick out tiny fecal pellets called frass that accumulate below infested wood.
entries.cicada: Periodical cicadas emerge in synchronized broods of billions after 13 or 17 years underground.
entries.dog-day-cicada: Dog-day cicadas get their name because they emerge during the dog days of summer.
entries.masked-devil-cicada: Some Australian cicada species have the loudest insect calls, exceeding 120 decibels.
entries.leafhopper: Brown planthoppers can jump 70 times their body length in a single leap.
entries.spittlebug: Spittlebug nymphs produce foamy saliva masses called cuckoo spit to protect themselves.
entries.aphid: Aphids can produce up to 80 offspring per female without mating through parthenogenesis.
entries.bed-bug: Bed bugs can survive for over a year without feeding and are resistant to many pesticides.
entries.kissing-bug: Kissing bugs are called so because they often bite people on the face while they sleep.
entries.stink-bug: Stink bugs release a foul-smelling chemical from glands on their thorax when disturbed.
entries.box-elder-bug: Box elder bugs aggregate in huge numbers on warm south-facing walls in autumn.
entries.water-strider: Water striders can walk on water due to microscopic hairs on their legs that trap air.
entries.giant-water-bug: Giant water bugs are called toe-biters and can deliver an extremely painful bite.
entries.american-grasshopper: Bird grasshoppers are strong fliers and can travel significant distances during migrations.
entries.desert-locust: Desert locust swarms can cover 460 square miles and contain 40 to 80 billion insects.
entries.mormon-cricket: Despite their name, Mormon crickets are actually shield-backed katydids, not true crickets.
entries.field-cricket: Male field crickets chirp by rubbing their wings together, and you can estimate temperature by counting chirps.
entries.katydid: Katydid songs are ultrasonic, making them difficult for humans to hear without special equipment.
entries.mole-cricket: Mole crickets can swim and fly, making them highly mobile pests of turfgrass.
entries.snowy-tree-cricket: The snowy tree cricket is known as the thermometer cricket because chirp rate correlates with temperature.
entries.human-head-louse: Head lice have been companions of humans for at least 10,000 years.
entries.body-louse: Body lice have been used to track human migration patterns through DNA analysis.
entries.human-flea: Fleas can jump up to 150 times their body length, equivalent to a human jumping over a skyscraper.
entries.cat-flea: Cat fleas are the most common flea species on domestic pets worldwide.
entries.oriental-rat-flea: The oriental rat flea was the primary vector of bubonic plague during the Black Death.
entries.brown-recluse-spider: Brown recluse venom can cause necrotic lesions that take months to heal.
entries.wolf-spider: Wolf spider mothers carry their egg sacs and spiderlings on their backs.
entries.jumping-spider: Jumping spiders have the best vision of any spider and can jump 50 times their body length.
entries.orb-weaver-spider: Orb weavers rebuild their webs almost every night, consuming the old silk to recycle the proteins.
entries.peacock-spider: Male peacock spiders perform elaborate dance displays with colorful abdominal flaps to court females.
entries.brazilian-wandering-spider: The Brazilian wandering spider has the most potent venom of any spider and is listed in Guinness World Records.
entries.emperor-scorpion: Emperor scorpions glow bright blue-green under ultraviolet light.
entries.bark-scorpion: Arizona bark scorpions are the most venomous scorpion in North America and can climb walls and ceilings.
entries.deathstalker-scorpion: The deathstalker's venom contains compounds being researched for use in cancer treatment.
entries.spotted-lanternfly: Spotted lanternflies can lay up to 50 eggs on almost any flat surface.
entries.wheel-bug: The wheel bug gets its name from the distinctive cogwheel-like crest on its thorax.
entries.sawfly: Sawfly larvae look like caterpillars but have more than five pairs of prolegs.
entries.antlion: Antlion larvae dig conical pit traps in sand to catch ants and other small insects.
entries.lacewing: Lacewing larvae are called aphid lions and can each consume 200 aphids per week.
entries.dobsonfly: Dobsonfly larvae, called hellgrammites, are indicators of good water quality.
entries.mayfly: Adult mayflies have vestigial mouthparts and cannot eat, living only long enough to mate.
entries.earwig: Earwig mothers guard their eggs and clean them to prevent fungal growth.
entries.silverfish: Silverfish are among the most primitive wingless insects, virtually unchanged for 400 million years.
entries.firebrat: Firebrats prefer temperatures above 90 degrees Fahrenheit and can survive scorching conditions.
entries.jumping-bristletail: Jumping bristletails are among the most ancient insects, with a fossil record dating back 400 million years.
entries.snakefly: Snakefly larvae can crawl backwards at high speed to escape threats.
entries.cuckoo-bumblebee-parasite: Some cuckoo bumblebee species have been reclassified as entirely separate species from their hosts.
entries.musk-bee: Musk bees produce a distinctive lemony scent when disturbed.
entries.alkali-bee: Alkali bees prefer salty, alkaline soil for nesting and can form massive aggregations.
entries.carpenter-ant: Carpenter ants do not eat wood but excavate it to create nesting galleries.
entries.pharaoh-ant: Pharaoh ants can nest in extremely small spaces and are known to spread disease in hospitals.
entries.odorous-house-ant: Odorous house ants smell like crushed coconut when squished.
entries.blue-ringed-octopus: Its venom contains tetrodotoxin, potent enough to kill 26 humans.
entries.mimic-octopus: Can impersonate over 15 different species including lionfish and sea snakes.
entries.colossal-squid: Has the largest eyes of any animal, up to 10 inches in diameter.
entries.humboldt-squid: Also called the jumbo squid or red devil for its aggressive nature.
entries.giant-squid: Was considered a mythical creature until first photographed alive in 2004.
entries.firefly-squid: Produces its own light through bioluminescent organs called photophores.
entries.caribbean-reef-octopus: Has two-thirds of its neurons in its arms rather than its brain.
entries.flamboyant-cuttlefish: One of only two known poisonous cephalopods.
entries.common-cuttlefish: Can hypnotize prey with rapidly changing color patterns.
entries.chambered-nautilus: Has remained virtually unchanged for over 500 million years.
entries.argonaut: Females create a paper-thin shell for egg protection, the only octopus to do so.
entries.vampire-squid: Is neither a true squid nor a true octopus but occupies its own order.
entries.strawberry-squid: Has photophores covering its body that produce a strawberry-red glow to camouflage against predators.
entries.cockatoo-squid: Inflates its body with seawater to appear larger and more intimidating to predators.
entries.pajama-squid: Has a distinctive black-and-white striped pattern resembling striped pajamas.
entries.bobtail-squid: Harbors bioluminescent bacteria in a specialized light organ for counter-illumination camouflage.
entries.pygmy-squid: Uses a sticky gland on its nose to attach itself to seagrass blades.
entries.american-lobster: Can live over 100 years and keep growing throughout its life.
entries.european-lobster: Can weigh up to 28 pounds and is one of the largest crustaceans in European waters.
entries.spiny-lobster: Lacks large claws and instead produces loud rasping sounds to deter predators.
entries.slipper-lobster: Has distinctive plate-like antennae that resemble slipper soles.
entries.mantis-shrimp: Can punch with the force of a .22 caliber bullet, breaking aquarium glass.
entries.peacock-mantis-shrimp: Can see 16 types of color receptors and perceives ultraviolet and polarized light.
entries.spearer-mantis-shrimp: Has barbed, spear-like appendages for impaling soft-bodied prey like fish.
entries.blue-crab: Named for its bright blue claws used in mating displays.
